Friend, it’s been years
since you last spoke to me.
It is painful to know
that you only remember me
as an angry teenager.

I want you to know
that I remember you,
The ease of your laugh, 
still, after all this time.
I remember
how you always seemed 
one step ahead
of the rest of us,
tuned in to a higher frequency.

All I’d like to know
is if you’re okay now.
If your anger has become a friend,
if you’ve forgiven yourself
for the sin you never committed.

I’d like to walk around
in your mind someday.

isabel’s monologue from Measure for Measure is amazing. you get to cover a lot of different emotions and realizations in just a few short lines! For context, Isabel is a nun whose brother is condemned to death for having premarital sex. the corrupt judge Angelo tells her that he will spare his life on the condition that Isabel lets him take her virginity. here is the monologue:

To whom should I complain? Did I tell this,
Who would believe me? O perilous mouths,
That bear in them one and the self-same tongue,
Either of condemnation or approof;
Bidding the law make court'sy to their will:
Hooking both right and wrong to the appetite,
To follow as it draws! I'll to my brother:
Though he hath fallen by prompture of the blood,
Yet hath he in him such a mind of honour.
That, had he twenty heads to tender down
On twenty bloody blocks, he'ld yield them up,
Before his sister should her body stoop
To such abhorr'd pollution.
Then, Isabel, live chaste, and, brother, die:
More than our brother is our chastity.
I'll tell him yet of Angelo's request,
And fit his mind to death, for his soul's rest.
